Today Apple rolled out significant price increases across most of its products, but certain products were spared. Here’s every Apple product that didn’t increase in price—at least not yet.

iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods models are not impacted by new price increases

Last week Apple CEO Tim Cook warned that product price increases were “unavoidable” due to the current AI-driven constraints on RAM and storage.

And today, the company officially rolled out those increases, with the vast majority of Apple products getting higher prices.

But select products are still the same price—at least for now.

New iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods models are unchanged in price, entirely avoiding the increases that hit every other product line. Accessories seem to be spared too.

These product lines avoided price increases across the board. Meaning there are no iPhone, Apple Watch, or AirPods models that got more expensive today. In total, that’s seven iPhones, three Apple Watches, and four AirPods models.

Meanwhile, all Macs, iPads, Home products, and Apple Vision Pro are now more expensive, effective immediately. Here’s the full list of impacted products.

Why did Apple’s price increases not affect iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods? It’s possible the company plans to wait until September. That’s when it will unveil next-gen models like iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4, and more.

Whatever the reason, if you’re in the market for a new iPhone, Apple Watch, or pair of AirPods, now might be a good time to buy.

Why do you think Apple spared the iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods from higher prices? Let us know in the comments.
